overview: Two opposite thyroid disorders, defined by whether the gland is producing too little or too much thyroid hormone.
genZNote: Hypothyroidism: metabolism running in slow motion. Hyperthyroidism: metabolism stuck on fast forward.

aspects.label: Effect on Metabolic Rate
aspects.valueA: Decreased metabolic rate — weight gain, fatigue, cold intolerance.
aspects.valueB: Increased metabolic rate — weight loss, restlessness, heat intolerance.

aspects.label: Example Condition
aspects.valueA: Iodine deficiency causing goitre; Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
aspects.valueB: Graves' disease, an autoimmune condition causing overactive thyroid.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Simple goitre from iodine deficiency is technically a form of hypothyroidism where the gland enlarges while trying (and failing) to make enough hormone.
overlay.memoryTrick: Hypo = too low, slow. Hyper = too high, fast.
overlay.commonMisconception: A goitre (enlarged thyroid) doesn't automatically mean hyperthyroidism — it can occur in both hypo- and hyperthyroid states, depending on the underlying cause.
